output.summary: KEP-4292 adds a `custom` flag to `kubectl debug` that takes a JSON (later YAML) file with a partial corev1.Container spec, which is strategic-merge-patched onto the container spec generated by the predefined profiles. It graduated to stable and was marked implemented for 1.33.
output.rationale: Users need to customize debug containers (env vars, volume mounts, security contexts, labels, image pull secrets) but adding a flag per field would make the command unmaintainable. The proposal therefore accepts a partial container spec and patches it over the predefined profile, with custom values overriding profile values on conflict. It limits scope to container spec because container is the largest common type across pod, node, and ephemeral container debugging.

alternatives.option: Add a dedicated kubectl debug flag for each field
alternatives.why_not: The readme says adding a new flag for every field puts the debug command at risk of an unmanageable and unmaintainable state.

alternatives.option: Make the custom profile JSON a full corev1.Container spec instead of a partial one
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers raised this as an alternative in PR #4293 discussion; the source does not record a reason it was rejected beyond the partial-spec design that was adopted.

alternatives.option: Extend customization to pod spec fields as well
alternatives.why_not: The readme states this feature focuses only on container spec customization; pod spec changes can be handled by a few flags such as annotations and labels.

evidence.quote: Adding a new flag for every field puts a debug command at risk of unmanageable and unmaintainable state from not only maintainers point of view but also users.

custom profile json is patched onto the latest version of container spec generated by predefined profiles. As a result, custom profiles always suppress the properties inside predefined profiles in cases of conflicts.
This feature focuses only on container spec customization and has no attempt to change the other fields in pod spec.
Now that this KEP has graduated to `stable`, could we update the KEP status in kep.yaml (here) from `implementable` to `implemented`?
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5057 marks the KEP as implemented. I think, we can close this issue as done.
